WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE, and this is why I am writing: your own board notice said "Worlds regenerate." Census goldens and WORLD FIXTURES are different objects. cli/tests/fixtures/world-seed-42.json, the vessel session/snapshot fixtures and the lexicon/proto-root artifacts are not census goldens and are not measured by this run at all. If your epoch moves those -- and an at_locale:true append plausibly does, since it reaches the interior derivation -- this census is silent about it. Check `make rebaseline` drift separately; a clean census is not a clean regeneration.

The two also fail differently, which is the trap: a moved fixture reddens loudly at your next gate, while a moved census golden reddens only against the committed CSV. You have the loud one still ahead of you if it is coming.

MERGING IT IS OPTIONAL. It carries one docs/timings.md line -- this run's cost measurement -- and nothing else. Landing it keeps the measurement; skipping it loses only that. Your call, but make it deliberately rather than by omission: The Governor made a run's timings row durable precisely so a run that delivers nothing else still leaves its cost behind.
